key_insight: Encoding site-projected orbital density of states (pDOS) into atomic graph nodes gives graph neural networks direct access to each atom’s electronic environment, improving materials-property prediction beyond static elemental descriptors.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical way to boost accuracy in computational materials design by injecting first-principles electronic-structure information into scalable graph models.
method: Compute pDOS fingerprints from DFT for each atomic site.
Fuse pDOS with Pettifor elemental embeddings before message passing in a graph neural network.
Use spectral attention gating to identify which orbitals and energy windows matter for each target property.
evidence_signal: Compared with an elemental-descriptor baseline, pDOS augmentation reduced prediction error by 22.9% for superconducting Tc and 27.9% for optical dielectric constant ε∞, with gains similar to doubling training data.
watch_item: Benefits depend on dataset size and pDOS feature length, so the approach may be less effective on small datasets such as Heusler magnetic exchange energies.
paper_title: Machine Learning Materials Properties by Encoding Orbital-Projected Density of States
